name: TDM-105795

card.summary: An investigational topical thyroid hormone receptor agonist from TechnoDerma Medicines, studied in men with pattern hair loss as a scalp solution to increase hair count.
card.note: Investigational; not an approved or marketed treatment.

quick.overview:
TDM-105795, also coded CU-40101, is an experimental scalp solution from the biotech TechnoDerma Medicines. The appearance goal is denser hair for people with androgenetic alopecia (pattern hair loss).

It is a small molecule that acts on thyroid hormone receptors, and the company reports that in a 2024-announced phase 2a trial in 71 men, hair counts rose more with the drug than with vehicle over four months.
quick.how: It is applied to the scalp as a topical solution in clinical trials, once daily in the phase 2a study. It is not an approved product, and trial participation is the only route to it.
quick.risks: Company-reported phase 1 and phase 2a results describe the drug as well tolerated with no significant safety concerns, and preclinical work suggested little systemic absorption. Thyroid hormone signalling has body-wide effects, so systemic exposure is the aspect researchers watch. Long-term safety has not been published in peer-reviewed form.

lead: TDM-105795, also listed as CU-40101, is an investigational topical drug for pattern hair loss, developed by TechnoDerma Medicines.[1][2] It is a small-molecule thyromimetic, meaning it activates thyroid hormone receptors, and it is formulated as a solution applied to the scalp.[1][2] The aim is a higher count of growing scalp hairs, giving a fuller look in people with androgenetic alopecia.

In June 2024 the company announced results of a randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled phase 2a study in 71 men: after four months of daily use, target-area hair count rose by an average of about 24 hairs per square centimetre on the higher strength and about 20 on the lower strength, against about 14 with vehicle.[2] The company reported both strengths were well tolerated.[2] These figures come from company communications rather than a peer-reviewed paper.
Hair-loss forum members have followed the compound since its first phase 1 dosing was reported in 2021, as a potential new mechanism alongside minoxidil and finasteride.[4]

chain: Topical thyromimetic applied to the scalp
Resting follicles are pushed toward the growth phase
Higher non-vellus hair count in the treated area
angle.text: The compound is intended to be applied to thinning areas of the scalp to increase the number of growing hairs. In the company-reported phase 2a trial, treated men gained more hairs per square centimetre than vehicle users; the effect on visible appearance has not been published in a peer-reviewed study.

paras: TDM-105795 is a small molecule with thyromimetic properties.[2] TechnoDerma Medicines, a privately held clinical-stage company that has worked from China and the United States, lists it as its lead topical candidate for androgenetic alopecia.[2][4] A drug-pipeline database classes it as a thyroid hormone receptor agonist for skin disorders and records the alternative codes CU-40101 and CU 40101-101.[1]

Thyroid hormones influence the hair cycle, and thyroid receptor agonists have been explored for hair loss for over a decade. A 2010 report described a beta-subtype-selective thyromimetic that stimulated hair growth in mouse and monkey models after topical application.[5] The company states that in mice TDM-105795 stimulated growth in a dose-dependent manner, likely by activating dormant follicle stem cells and moving resting follicles into the growth (anagen) phase.[2] Preclinical work also suggested minimal systemic absorption and a short elimination half-life, which the company says may lower systemic risk.[2]

A phase 1 trial registered by TechnoDerma assessed safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics of the solution in healthy men aged 18 to 55 with moderate-to-severe androgenetic alopecia (Norwood-Hamilton III to VI), planned at 32 participants over 14 weeks at two sites; the registry lists it as completed without posted results.[3]

The phase 2a study was randomized 1:1:1 across two strengths and vehicle, with daily application for four months at 13 US sites in 71 men, assessing efficacy, safety and pharmacokinetics.[2] According to the company's June 2024 announcement, non-vellus target-area hair count rose by 24.3 hairs/cm2 at 0.02%, 20.3 at 0.0025% and 14.0 with placebo, with no significant safety concerns.[2] A drug database also lists a phase 1 programme in China as of September 2025.[1]

Studies of related thyroid-pathway compounds include a 2022 mouse paper on a different thyroid receptor agonist, TDM10842, which concluded it accelerated entry into anagen, and a 2024 ex vivo study in which topical T3 and T4 increased the share of anagen follicles in cultured human scalp skin.[6] These are not studies of TDM-105795.
TDM-105795 has not been approved by any regulator. Public information on its development comes mainly from company releases, trial registries and a pipeline database.

timeline.event: A beta-selective thyromimetic is reported to grow hair in mouse and monkey models after topical use.[5]
First patients are reported dosed in a phase 1 trial in healthy men with androgenetic alopecia.[4]
The phase 1 registry record is listed as completed.[3]
TechnoDerma announces phase 2a results in 71 men.[2]
A pipeline database records a phase 1 programme in China.[1]

lore.intro: On hair-loss forums, TDM-105795 has been discussed since 2021 as a possible next-generation topical, with members tracking trial news and comparing the reported hair counts with those of existing treatments.[4]

claims.claim: It could become a new topical option alongside minoxidil and finasteride
claims.believers: Forum members see a drug already in human trials with a novel mechanism as a hopeful development and some tried to enrol in the first trial.[4]
claims.experts: The company reports positive phase 2a hair-count results with good tolerability; peer-reviewed results and larger trials have not been published.[2]

claims.claim: The older thyroid-agonist research is the basis for the drug
claims.believers: Early threads linked a published thyroid receptor agonist paper to the compound.[4]
claims.experts: Other forum members noted that paper was not directly tied to TDM-105795, and the company has described the compound as its own.[4][5]
